llm.summary: This is a disclosed natural-language wrapper for a resilience monitoring plugin, with some broad trigger phrases but no artifact-backed hidden or malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is LLM API error monitoring, retry strategy management, reporting, and dashboard access; the documented tools and bundled dashboard assets match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Some Chinese activation examples are generic, such as opening a monitoring panel, which could cause accidental routing, but the mapped actions are disclosed and fit the resilience dashboard use case.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly requires installing a separate @leiJack-lo/resilience plugin with --dangerously-force-unsafe-install and discloses why: browser launching, a local HTTP server, hooks, and local log/config writes.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifacts describe local dashboard access on 127.0.0.1, local OpenClaw configuration, and per-instance local storage, which are proportionate to the monitoring purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The required plugin is documented as registering gateway hooks, auto-starting a dashboard by default, and persisting logs/statistics/strategies under ~/.openclaw/plugins/resilience; this is sensitive but disclosed and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only if you intend to use the companion resilience plugin and are comfortable with it running gateway hooks, starting a local dashboard, and storing API error/retry data locally. Consider using explicit resilience-related commands to avoid accidental dashboard opening or retry-strategy changes.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The examples around SKILL.md lines 28-32 are resilience/error-monitoring examples, including a disclosed retry-policy update; they could be narrower, but they are not hidden or purpose-mismatched.
[SQP-1] expected: The dashboard phrases around SKILL.md lines 68-71 include generic wording, but opening the local resilience dashboard is an expected capability and is documented as such.
[SQP-1] expected: The skill.json natural-language mappings include broad dashboard-opening intents; this is a routing-quality concern, not evidence of deception, exfiltration, or destructive behavior.
